newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, aided by dollar's rise.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, aided by dollar's rise.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing, as a sharp rally in the Canadian dollar helped spur buying across the curve, dealers said.

"There was a lot of good European buying of Canadian dollars and I think some of it's been coming into the debt market, especially the shorter end of the curve," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analysts with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.10 to C$108.40 to yield 7.278 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.79 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 49 basis points from 51 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canada's dollar rallied by more than a full Canadian cent to end at C$1.3413 (US$0.7456) on Wednesday from Tuesday's close at C$1.3519 (US$0.7397). Most of the buying interest came from Europe following a bullish story on Canada in the Financial Times.
The rally in the currency was so strong it prompted the Bank of Canada to intervene on currency markets, selling Canadian dollars for U.S. dollars.
"There was no real data or news otherwise to really have a fundamental effect. It was just a flows type of environment starting over from Europe," said Kalirai.
In new issue news, Canada Trustco Mortgage Co, a unit of CT Financial Services Inc, set C$400 million in new bonds on financial markets.

The first tranche of the issue, C$250 million in 5.2 percent bonds due January 31, 2000, was priced at C$99.896 with a yield of 5.237. A second tranche of C$150 million in 6.05 percent bonds due January 31, 2002, was priced at C$99.805 with a yield of 6.095 percent.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.12 to C$102.75 to yield 6.614 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bond narrowed to nine basis points from 11 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.85 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.14 percent.
